REST API Reference

Complete REST API reference for OpenAPI CLI.

Overview

OpenAPI CLI provides a REST API for programmatic access to all CLI functionality through HTTP endpoints. The REST API is useful for: - Building custom integrations - Automating workflows via webhooks - Creating custom UIs - Service-to-service communication

Base URL

Default: http://localhost:8080

Configurable via configuration:

mcp:
  enabled: true
  port: 8080
  host: 0.0.0.0

Authentication

The REST API supports multiple authentication methods.

API Key Authentication

curl -H "X-API-Key: your-secret-key" http://localhost:8080/spec/validate

Configuration:

auth:
  type: apikey
  apikey:
    header: X-API-Key
    value: ${API_KEY}

OAuth2 Bearer Token

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" http://localhost:8080/spec/validate

Configuration:

auth:
  type: oauth2
  oauth2:
    token_url: https://auth.example.com/oauth/token
    scopes:
      - read
      - write

API Endpoints

Root Endpoint

Get API information.

GET /

Response:

{
  "name": "openapi-cli",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "endpoints": ["/spec", "/commands", "/api"],
  "documentation": "/docs"
}

Specification Endpoints

Validate OpenAPI Spec

Validate an OpenAPI specification.

POST /spec/validate

Request Body:

{
  "spec": "<OpenAPI spec content>",
  "strict": false
}

Response:

{
  "valid": true,
  "errors": []
}

Example:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/spec/validate \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"spec":"openapi: 3.0.3\ninfo:\n  title: Test\npaths: {}"}'

Get Spec Info

Get information about an OpenAPI specification.

GET /spec/info?spec=<spec-path>

Response:

{
  "title": "PetStore API",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Sample PetStore API",
  "endpoints": 20,
  "paths": {
    "/pet": ["GET", "POST"],
    "/pet/{petId}": ["GET", "PUT", "DELETE"]
  }
}

Convert Spec Format

Convert between OpenAPI formats.

POST /spec/convert

Request Body:

{
  "spec": "<spec content>",
  "fromFormat": "json",
  "toFormat": "yaml"
}

Response:

{
  "spec": "<converted spec>",
  "format": "yaml"
}

CLI Command Endpoints

List Commands

List all available CLI commands.

GET /commands

Response:

{
  "commands": [
    {
      "name": "generate",
      "description": "Generate CLI commands from spec",
      "usage": "openapi-cli generate <spec-path-or-url>"
    },
    {
      "name": "inventory list",
      "description": "List configured inventories",
      "usage": "openapi-cli inventory list"
    }
  ]
}

Execute Command

Execute a CLI command via REST API.

POST /commands/execute

Request Body:

{
  "command": "generate",
  "args": ["petstore.json"],
  "options": {
    "baseUrl": "https://api.example.com",
    "verbose": true
  }
}

Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "exitCode": 0,
  "stdout": "Commands generated from petstore.json",
  "stderr": ""
}

Example:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/commands/execute \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "command": "inventory list",
    "args": [],
    "options": {"format": "json"}
  }'

API Request Endpoints

Make API Request

Make a request to the target API.

POST /api/request

Request Body:

{
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/pet/1",
  "baseUrl": "https://api.example.com/v1",
  "headers": {
    "Authorization": "Bearer token"
  },
  "query": {
    "fields": "id,name"
  }
}

Response:

{
  "status": 200,
  "headers": {
    "Content-Type": "application/json"
  },
  "body": {
    "id": 1,
    "name": "Fluffy"
  }
}

Batch Requests

Make multiple API requests in parallel.

POST /api/batch

Request Body:

{
  "requests": [
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/pet/1"
    },
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/pet/2"
    }
  ]
}

Response:

{
  "results": [
    {
      "status": 200,
      "body": {"id": 1, "name": "Fluffy"}
    },
    {
      "status": 200,
      "body": {"id": 2, "name": "Rex"}
    }
  ]
}

Documentation Endpoints

Generate Documentation

Generate API documentation.

POST /docs/generate

Request Body:

{
  "spec": "<OpenAPI spec>",
  "format": "markdown",
  "output": "/path/to/docs"
}

Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "files": [
    "/path/to/docs/index.md",
    "/path/to/docs/api.md"
  ]
}

Serve Documentation

Serve documentation files.

GET /docs/{path}

Example:

curl http://localhost:8080/docs/index.md

Configuration Endpoints

Get Configuration

Get current configuration.

GET /config

Response:

{
  "spec": {
    "path": "openapi.json",
    "baseUrl": "https://api.example.com/v1"
  },
  "http": {
    "timeout": "30s",
    "verifySsl": true
  },
  "output": {
    "format": "table"
  }
}

Update Configuration

Update configuration values.

PUT /config

Request Body:

{
  "http": {
    "timeout": "60s"
  },
  "output": {
    "format": "json"
  }
}

Response:

{
  "success": true
}

Validate Configuration

Validate current configuration.

POST /config/validate

Response:

{
  "valid": true,
  "errors": []
}

Cache Endpoints

Get Cache Stats

Get cache statistics.

GET /cache/stats

Response:

{
  "hits": 150,
  "misses": 30,
  "size": "100MB",
  "items": 500
}

Clear Cache

Clear the cache.

DELETE /cache

Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "cleared": 500
}

Authentication Endpoints

Get Auth Status

Check authentication status.

GET /auth/status

Response:

{
  "authenticated": true,
  "provider": "oauth2",
  "expires": "2026-03-03T10:00:00Z"
}

Login

Authenticate with OAuth2.

POST /auth/login

Request Body:

{
  "provider": "google",
  "clientId": "your-client-id",
  "scopes": ["read", "write"]
}

Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "token": "access_token"
}

Logout

Logout and clear credentials.

POST /auth/logout

Response:

{
  "success": true
}

Health Endpoint

Check service health.

GET /health

Response:

{
  "status": "healthy",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "uptime": "3600s"
}

Error Responses

All endpoints return errors in this format:

{
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_SPEC",
    "message": "OpenAPI specification is invalid",
    "details": {
      "line": 10,
      "column": 5,
      "error": "Missing required field"
    }
  }
}

Error Codes

Code HTTP Status Description
INVALID_SPEC 400 Invalid OpenAPI specification
AUTH_FAILED 401 Authentication failed
NOT_FOUND 404 Resource not found
VALIDATION_ERROR 422 Request validation failed
TIMEOUT 408 Request timeout
SERVER_ERROR 500 Internal server error

Rate Limiting

The REST API includes rate limiting to prevent abuse:

Default Configuration:

rate_limit:
  enabled: true
  requests_per_second: 10
  burst: 100
  algorithm: token_bucket

Rate Limit Headers

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1648867200

Rate Limit Response

{
  "error": {
    "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
    "message": "Rate limit exceeded. Please retry later."
  }
}

CORS Support

Configure CORS for cross-origin requests:

mcp:
  cors:
    enabled: true
    allowed_origins:
      - "http://localhost:3000"
      - "https://yourdomain.com"
    allowed_methods:
      - GET
      - POST
      - PUT
      - DELETE
    allowed_headers:
      - Content-Type
      - Authorization
    max_age: 3600

Webhooks

Configure webhooks for event notifications.

Register Webhook

POST /webhooks

Request Body:

{
  "url": "https://yourdomain.com/webhook",
  "events": [
    "api.request",
    "api.error"
  ],
  "secret": "webhook-secret"
}

Response:

{
  "webhookId": "wh_12345",
  "status": "active"
}

Webhook Events

Event Description
api.request API request made
api.response API response received
api.error API error occurred
spec.loaded Specification loaded
command.executed CLI command executed

Webhook Payload

{
  "event": "api.request",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-02T10:00:00Z",
  "data": {
    "method": "GET",
    "path": "/pet/1",
    "headers": {}
  }
}

WebSocket Support

Real-time event streaming via WebSocket.

Connect to WebSocket

const ws = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:8080/events');

ws.onmessage = (event) => {
  const data = JSON.parse(event.data);
  console.log('Event:', data.event, data);
};

// Subscribe to events
ws.send(JSON.stringify({
  action: 'subscribe',
  events: ['api.request', 'api.response']
}));

Examples

Example 1: Validate Spec

# Validate OpenAPI spec
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/spec/validate \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @spec.json

Example 2: Get Inventory

# List API resources
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/commands/execute \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: your-secret" \
  -d '{
    "command": "inventory list",
    "args": [],
    "options": {"format": "json"}
  }'

Example 3: Make API Request

# Make a single API request
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/request \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: your-secret" \
  -d '{
    "method": "GET",
    "path": "/pet/1",
    "baseUrl": "https://petstore.swagger.io/v2"
  }'

Example 4: Batch Requests

# Make multiple API requests
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/batch \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: your-secret" \
  -d '{
    "requests": [
      {"method": "GET", "path": "/pet/1"},
      {"method": "GET", "path": "/pet/2"},
      {"method": "GET", "path": "/pet/3"}
    ]
  }'

Example 5: Get Configuration

# Get current configuration
curl http://localhost:8080/config \
  -H "X-API-Key: your-secret"

Example 6: Update Configuration

# Update timeout setting
curl -X PUT http://localhost:8080/config \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: your-secret" \
  -d '{"http": {"timeout": "60s"}}'

Example 7: Health Check

# Check service health
curl http://localhost:8080/health

Example 8: Clear Cache

# Clear cache
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/cache \
  -H "X-API-Key: your-secret"

Configuration

Enable REST API

mcp:
  enabled: true
  port: 8080
  host: 0.0.0.0

rest:
  enabled: true
  cors:
    enabled: true
  rate_limit:
    enabled: true
    requests_per_second: 10

Authentication Settings

auth:
  type: apikey
  apikey:
    header: X-API-Key
    value: ${API_KEY}

Security

Recommendations

  1. Use HTTPS in production
  2. Enable rate limiting to prevent abuse
  3. Use strong secrets for API keys
  4. Validate all inputs before processing
  5. Log all requests for audit trails
  6. Enable CORS only for trusted origins

Best Practices

  • Store secrets in environment variables
  • Use short-lived tokens
  • Rotate credentials regularly
  • Audit webhook endpoints
  • Monitor for suspicious activity

Testing

Manual Testing

# Health check
curl http://localhost:8080/health

# Validate spec
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/spec/validate -d @spec.json

# Make request
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/commands/execute \
  -d '{"command": "inventory list", "args": []}'

Automated Testing with curl

#!/bin/bash

# Test suite
echo "Testing REST API..."

# Health check
curl -f http://localhost:8080/health || exit 1

# Validate spec
curl -f -X POST http://localhost:8080/spec/validate \
  -d @valid_spec.json || exit 1

# Make request
curl -f -X POST http://localhost:8080/commands/execute \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  -d '{"command": "version"}' || exit 1

echo "All tests passed!"

Troubleshooting

Connection Refused

Issue: curl: (7) Failed to connect to localhost port 8080

Solution: Ensure the REST API is enabled and running:

# Ensure the MCP server is built and running:
make build
./bin/openapi-mcp --port 8080

Authentication Failed

Issue: {"error":{"code":"AUTH_FAILED"}}

Solution: Verify your API key:

# Set API key
export API_KEY=your-secret

# Make request
curl -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" http://localhost:8080/health

Rate Limit Exceeded

Issue: {"error":{"code":"RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED"}}

Solution: Wait and retry, or adjust rate limits:

rate_limit:
  requests_per_second: 20
  burst: 200
